text: In 1932, Australia went to war with emus.
Soldiers. Machine guns. Ten thousand bullets. And the farmers paid for the bullets.
The gun jammed. A politician said the emus deserved medals. The army pulled out.
By the headlines, Australia lost a war to birds.
So the farmers took over. The government paid a bounty for every beak.
One count says over fifty-seven thousand emus, in a single season.
The army managed under a thousand, by its own count.
The winning weapon wasn't a machine gun. It was a payment per beak.
